nodes.label: YouTube IFrame Player error 153
nodes.summary: Independent external re-verification of the same defect, from a read-only audit subagent. Tauri issue tauri-apps/tauri#14422 is labelled platform: Linux AND platform: macOS, so it is explicitly not a Linux-specific failure: dev mode over http://localhost:1430 works, production over the custom scheme tauri://localhost fails with 153. Five remedies all failed (playerVars.origin set to own origin, origin set to an HTTP localhost value, hand-built iframe with origin in the query string, referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin", iv_load_policy). Snipset's situation is called architecturally identical: tauri.conf.json:8 devUrl http://localhost:1420 versus frontendDist on the snipset: scheme. The Discourse/Anvil/NewsBlur reports that resolve 153 by ADDING referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" are refuted here, because that only helps a page that already has an HTTP origin to report. The issue is Closed with no stated resolution. Residual caveat stated honestly: one older report has an iframe loading on Ubuntu/WebKitGTK but never playing while the same code works on Windows, so a second WebKit-specific failure mode cannot be excluded.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r6-precedent-and-alternative-audit [ses_f24bc0786ffepEZYl6g8AsbFaj].md:L7338] The verdict is that "custom scheme carries no Referer" is the better-supported explanation for 153, not Linux being unsupported entirely

nodes.label: No extraction-free path to YouTube audio in a webview exists
nodes.norm_label: no extraction free path to youtube audio in a webview exists
nodes.summary: The audit's answer to "can a plain HTMLAudioElement play YouTube DASH/HLS directly, with no extraction tool": definitively no, at high confidence. Three independent blocks. (1) YouTube publishes no stable unsigned direct audio URL: stream URLs come out of the internal player API signed and IP-bound, requiring the n and increasingly pot challenge parameters, which are computed by executing YouTube's own player JavaScript; without a JS runtime yt-dlp reports "n challenge solving failed: Some formats may be missing", and as of 2025.11.12 upstream states support for YouTube without a JavaScript runtime is deprecated and that it is expected support will not be possible at all without a JS runtime. (2) DASH cannot be handed to an <audio> element even in principle: per MDN, no browser has native support for DASH, and you must run dash.js against an .mpd you host yourself. (3) YouTube ToS reserves access, reproduce, download, distribute except as expressly authorised. m3u8/HLS audio-only formats do appear in some yt-dlp format listings but come through the same signed-URL plus challenge pipeline, are not universally present, and Safari is the only engine guaranteed to consume them; WebKitGTK will not.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r6-precedent-and-alternative-audit [ses_f24bc0786ffepEZYl6g8AsbFaj].md:L7336] Any working YouTube audio in a webview requires an extraction/injection component, which is exactly the cost the decision was trying to price

nodes.label: Tauri asset protocol scope is $DOWNLOAD and $APP only, so a temp-file cannot be played
nodes.norm_label: tauri asset protocol scope is download and app only so a temp file cannot be played
nodes.summary: apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:27-30 sets "assetProtocol": { "enable": true, "scope": ["$DOWNLOAD/**", "$APP/**"] }. Only the OS Downloads dir and the app dir are readable via http://asset.localhost, so a file written to /tmp or $TEMP cannot be played through resolveAudioSourceUrl. The audit calls this the single hardest blocker for the naive "extract to temp, point asset.localhost at it" design. A contract test, apps/web/src/__contract__/tauriConfig.test.ts:39-57, asserts enable === true, asserts the scope never contains a literal **, and asserts every scope prefix is in an allowlist at :30-34 ($APPCACHE, $APP, $RESOURCE, $EXE, plus $DOWNLOAD), so adding $TEMP/** would require updating that allowlist. convertFileSrc (used at apps/web/src/components/DownloadsMagicMenu.tsx:239) is bound by the same scope.

nodes.label: The File to Blob to blob: URL path bypasses the asset protocol scope entirely
nodes.norm_label: the file to blob to blob url path bypasses the asset protocol scope entirely
nodes.summary: The audit's most important Part A finding: local-file playback already works on Linux with zero permissions. apps/web/src/pages/pomodoro/PomodoroMusicBar.tsx:296-335 handleFileSelect does const blobUrl = URL.createObjectURL(file) at :311, then sourceType: "local", sourceUrlOrPath: blobUrl at :316-317, then setTrack + play at :330-331, triggered by a hidden input type="file" accept="audio/*" at :759-765 and a Browse button at :766-777. The browser File to Blob to blob: URL shape completely bypasses the Tauri asset protocol and its scope, so any arbitrary audio file on disk is playable today. The engine already supports it: pomodoroMusicPlayer.ts:552-555 assigns currentBlobUrl for revocation, with revokeBlobUrl() at :212-223. The audit also notes capabilities/default.json:46-57 already grants fs:allow-read-file over $TEMP/** and **, so Rust can write to $TEMP and the frontend can readFile the bytes and build the same Blob, with no permission change.

nodes.label: rodio is pinned to vorbis and wav only, so the Rust side cannot decode MP3, AAC or Opus
nodes.norm_label: rodio is pinned to vorbis and wav only so the rust side cannot decode mp3 aac or opus
nodes.summary: apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:109 and :123 pin rodio = { version = "0.22", default-features = false, features = ["playback", "vorbis", "wav"] }. The consequence the audit draws is that a Rust-side decoder can read only OGG/Vorbis and WAV and cannot decode MP3, AAC or Opus, which removes rodio as any help for a YouTube extraction path. symphonia appears in Cargo.lock:6704-6795 only as a transitive dep of rodio, not a direct dependency. whisper-rs (Cargo.lock:8443) is STT-only, in speech/stt/whisper_engine.rs, and unrelated to playback.

nodes.label: The repo's only ffmpeg reference is an opportunistic PATH probe, not a declared dependency
nodes.norm_label: the repos only ffmpeg reference is an opportunistic path probe not a declared dependency
nodes.summary: A previous commit's mention of "Invoke ffmpeg bundled via yt-dlp skill requirements" in apps/chrome-clipboard-bridge/host/host.ts:154-155 is the only ffmpeg reference in the whole repo. It shells bare ffmpeg from PATH via Bun $ to extract one video frame as a PNG thumbnail for a wl-copy clipboard write on WSL, wrapped in a try/catch that rethrows as a clipboard failure at :159-163. The audit's verified negatives: no ffmpeg or yt-dlp in any package.json, zero matches in scripts/**, nothing in any Dockerfile/deb/AppImage spec, nothing in Cargo.toml. It is an opportunistic PATH probe with no declared dependency, no version pin, no install path and no packaging guarantee, and the comment refers to an external agent skill's requirement rather than this repo's. The audit states plainly that ffmpeg is NOT a repo assumption and treating it as one would be a false precedent. Separately: no downloader or extractor exists, no yt-dlp binding, no MP4Box/libav/FFI, and tauri_plugin_shell is not registered in lib.rs:372-380 and there is no shell: permission in capabilities/default.json, though plain Command::new("git") subprocess spawning already exists (activity/git_context.rs:20,32,41).

nodes.label: Gating a media source on canPlayType beats branching on an OS string
nodes.norm_label: gating a media source on canplaytype beats branching on an os string
nodes.summary: A4 of the audit finds two established platform-detection conventions, both of which a new Linux branch should follow rather than inventing a helper: Rust compile-time cfg!(target_os = "linux") (canonical worked example setup/graphics.rs:164, where the Windows-only Graphics feature is gated by a single platform_supported boolean surfaced as GraphicsStatus.platform_supported at :183-184), and frontend runtime isWindowsPlatform() at useGraphicsSettings.ts:14-20 using navigator.userAgent plus optional navigator.userAgentData.platform. There is no isLinuxPlatform() and no shared utils/platform.ts. The audit recommends a third thing as better than either: apps/web/src/utils/mediaPlayback.ts:8 canPlayMimeType(mime, kind), which builds a detached audio/video element and calls canPlayType, failing open, and is already used at ChatMessages.tsx:85,94,109,111 and chat/ChatActionCards.tsx:244,253,262,263 to hide playback UI for unplayable media. Gating the music source on canPlayMimeType("audio/mpeg","audio") rather than on an OS string is the more portable pattern.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - r6-precedent-and-alternative-audit [ses_f24bc0786ffepEZYl6g8AsbFaj].md:L7307] Capability probing is preferred over an OS string because it also covers Linux distros with or without gst-plugins-ugly

nodes.label: Source version vs published version
nodes.summary: The concrete instance the website must encode: Windows SOURCE version is 0.6.849 while the Windows PUBLISHED installer is 0.6.838. Published versions are Windows 0.6.838 (NSIS exe plus portable), Linux 0.6.849 (AppImage), Android 1.0.6 (apk, versionCode 107). The website must show the published version for a download or a fact about a released installer, never the source version; the brief calls this the single most important correctness rule in the task. The regression evidence: platformReleaseFacts.windows.version === "0.6.838" and !== "0.6.849", asserted equal to releases/windows/latest.json version; platformReleaseFacts.linux.version === "0.6.849"; releaseFacts.latestWindows.version === "v0.6.838"; changelogData[0].version === "v0.6.838"; and versionLiterals() (regex \d+\.\d+\.\d+) returns [] for all four pages about.astro, id/about.astro, download.astro and id/download.astro, so no page can hard-code any version.

nodes.label: Per-platform release facts replace the single unlabeled version scalar
nodes.norm_label: per platform release facts replace the single unlabeled version scalar
nodes.summary: Contract item 1 of T11: releaseFacts.ts should give consumers a truthful, per-platform view of released version, date and checksums instead of the single scalar they assume today, and every old scalar consumer must be migrated explicitly. The RED evidence shows what the old shape was: the unlabeled scalar had to be gone ("expected { version: 'v0.6.838', ...(1) } to be undefined") and platformReleaseFacts had to be exported. Ten consumers were migrated and listed one line each, including releaseFacts.latest deleted in favour of three platformReleaseFacts[platform] chips, firstPublic renamed firstPublicWindows, count renamed windowsReleaseCount, the bare performance chip relabelled "Windows installer, measured per release", and DownloadGate.tsx's inline scalar chain replaced by an exported resolveDownloadTarget returning {platform, format, url}. The known cost, stated in the remaining-risks section: platformReleaseFacts transcribes the three manifests into a TS module by hand, and although two suites diff it against releases/<platform>/latest.json so a drifting release fails loudly, it is a manual edit rather than generated.

nodes.label: Any default Windows view must be labeled as Windows, never as a generic latest version
nodes.norm_label: a default windows view must be labeled as windows never as a generic latest version
nodes.summary: Contract item 4: any default Windows view must be labeled as Windows; a Windows number must not be presented as a generic "latest version". The implementation evidence: the download gate's default view is data-download-platform="windows", the visible badge reads "Windows 10/11", an assertion asserts the gate text contains no "latest version" copy, and resolveDownloadTarget returns platform: "windows" for msi and exe from any requester OS. The Windows checksum artifact names are asserted not to contain 0.6.849. Related to the source/published split: a labeled Windows view is what makes the 0.6.838 versus 0.6.849 confusion visible on the page rather than hidden in a scalar.

nodes.label: Locale-pair parity is compared as extracted shapes, proven non-vacuous by mutating one locale
nodes.norm_label: locale pair parity is compared as extracted shapes proven non vacuous by mutating one locale
nodes.summary: Contract item 3 requires EN and ID variants to stay consistent across about.astro/download.astro and id/about.astro/id/download.astro. The test compares five extracted shapes per page pair: platformTokens (explicit platform keys), versionLiterals, downloadEndpoints (the /api/updater/<name> set), sharedDataExpressions (a MULTISET of every platformReleaseFacts, releaseFacts, RELEASE_PLATFORMS and PLATFORM_LABELS expression including property paths), and benchmarkExpressions (the set of performance.* property paths). Each locale must also reference all of platformReleaseFacts, RELEASE_PLATFORMS and PLATFORM_LABELS, must call RELEASE_PLATFORMS.map(, and must contain the literal Windows. Non-vacuity is proven by a negative probe: mutating id/download.astro's endpoint apk to apk2 produced 2 failures, and changing id/about.astro's PLATFORM_LABELS[platform] label to platform while dropping performance.measuredAt produced 1 failure; both were restored from backups and the final run is 16/16 green.

nodes.label: T12's per-platform checksum merge clobbers the file, so it cannot be a reliable per-platform checksum source
nodes.norm_label: t12s per platform checksum merge clobbers the file so it cannot be a reliable per platform checksum source
nodes.summary: scripts/release/update-release-checksums.mjs was made platform-scoped by T12, but its mergePlatformChecksumRecord writes base[block.platform] = {...} and then overwrites base.windows with the legacy {msi, exe} map, while base.platform and base.artifacts remain single scalars clobbered by whichever platform ran last. So apps/website/src/data/release-checksums.json and apps/website/public/checksums.json cannot be a reliable per-platform source beyond the top-level version plus the windows block. The generator also hashes artifacts over the network (calculateRemoteSha256 via fetch) and its buildPlatformChecksumBlock hard-refuses a missing, empty or all-zero digest with E_CHECKSUM_UNKNOWN and E_CHECKSUM_PLACEHOLDER, so offline the only way to add a Linux or Android block would be to invent a hash, which the brief forbids and the generator exists to prevent. The consequence recorded: releaseFacts.ts reads the real Windows digests from the existing windows block and reports checksums: null for Linux and Android, with tests asserting exactly that and asserting no Windows digest appears in the Linux or Android facts. Both JSON files were left untouched, neither generated nor hand-edited.
